knowledgePattern: Convert a ceiling integral to a weighted geometric sum and shift it
solution:
For k−1<x≤k, the ceiling is k. Each interval has width 1, so the integral is S=∑k=120k2k. Values at isolated endpoints do not affect its area.

Write 2S=∑k=221(k−1)2k and subtract S. For each common power, the coefficients differ by one, giving S=20·221−∑k=1202k.

The remaining geometric sum is 221−2. Therefore S=19·221+2. Answer D.

hints.title: Split at the integer inputs
hints.body: On each interval between consecutive integers, determine the constant height of the integrand and the width of its rectangle.
hints.recap: A definite integral can be split into intervals on which the formula is simpler.
hints.pitfall: The ceiling at one isolated endpoint does not change an area.
hints.pause: Write the integral as a finite sum with correct first and last terms.

recall.reminder: A definite integral can be split into intervals on which the formula is simpler.

hints.title: Shift the weighted series
hints.body: Call the sum S. Write both S and 2S with their powers of 2 aligned, then subtract.
hints.recap: Rearrange an identity by collecting the same expression on one side; preserve signs when subtracting complete expressions.
hints.pitfall: Keep the shifted last term; it has no partner in the original sum.
hints.pause: Identify the surviving end terms and the simpler middle sum.

recall.reminder: Rearrange an identity by collecting the same expression on one side; preserve signs when subtracting complete expressions.

hints.title: Finish the remaining geometric sum
hints.body: Use the first term, ratio and number of terms of the unweighted sum left after subtraction.
hints.recap: A finite geometric sum must use its actual first term and inclusive term count.
hints.pitfall: The original weighted sum is not itself a geometric progression.
hints.pause: Evaluate the remaining sum and simplify the result exactly.
